ma_rockport_south_woods.blurb: Rockport South Woods is a bouldering-only zone in the woods of Rockport, on Cape Ann along Massachusetts' North Shore. Cape Ann as a whole is known for granite boulders and short cliffs. Problems here run from V0 to V7, with most of them between V3 and V5 and a smaller number of easier and harder ones on either side. The zone is split into roughly a dozen sub-areas. Town Line Boulders, also called South Woods, holds the most climbs, spread over a dozen or so blocks with fairly short approaches. Megatron Area sits in the middle of the woods near Rum Rock Lake and has its problems on five boulders. Cape Pond Boulders and Thatcher Road Boulders add smaller clusters.

wa_lower_lump_area.blurb: Lower Lump is a forested crag of about 20 acres at Index, in Washington's Skykomish Valley, next to the Lower Town Wall and close to the road and the railway tracks. The terrain runs from slab to roof. Climbing is mostly sport with some trad, at grades from 5.7 to 5.12, centred on 5.10 and with a good number of moderates. Beetle Bailey Slab holds the most climbs, and its base is shaded by large maples. Field of Dreams, The Wart and Tiki Heads are sport-focused walls, and Walking Legend Wall adds a smaller set of routes. The walk in from the nearest turnout takes under ten minutes.

wv_south_peak_west_face.blurb: The west face of South Peak is part of Seneca Rocks, in West Virginia's Monongahela National Forest east of Elkins. The face is highly featured and often exposed, and it looks out toward the visitor center. Seneca Rocks itself is white Tuscarora quartzite, with comfortable temperatures in spring, summer and fall. Climbing on the west face is overwhelmingly trad with a handful of sport routes, from 5.2 up to the low 5.12s, though most routes fall between 5.7 and 5.10. South Peak West Face (Main Area) holds the vast majority of the climbs, with Southwest Corner and The Old Hemlock Grove making up the rest.

wv_valley_falls_state_park.blurb: Valley Falls State Park lies along the Tygart Valley River near Fairmont, in northern West Virginia. The climbing here is all bouldering, from VB to V8, with most problems at V3 and under and a handful of hard ones above. The boulders sit on ridges above the river, and the approach trails are long and steep. The Main Area holds the most climbs, mostly along the trail, followed by East Boulders, Lost Cave Boulders and Roadside Boulders. The park is described as a smaller counterpart to Coopers Rock, with fewer boulders in less concentration.

wi_necedah_petenwell_rock.blurb: Necedah, also called Petenwell Rock, is a sandstone crag in central Wisconsin, about three miles east of the town of Necedah, beside the Wisconsin River and Petenwell Lake. The walls rise over 100 ft above the water in colorful sandstone that ranges from very hard to soft in places, and the towers stand on what was once the bed of Glacial Lake Wisconsin. Both sport and trad climbing are found here, along with a few top-ropes and boulder problems. Grades run from about 5.3 into the low 5.13s, with most routes between 5.8 and 5.11. Y-Crack Wall holds the most climbs, followed by Hell Wall (Quarry Wall), Anthrax Wall and Above Anthrax.

ab_nordegg_david_thompson_corridor.blurb: Nordegg and the David Thompson Corridor are a string of climbing areas along the highway in central Alberta, from Nordegg north to Highway 93, about an hour and three-quarters west of Red Deer. The corridor also has ice and multi-pitch climbing, but the rock climbing is mostly sport, with some trad and top-rope, mainly 5.10 to 5.12 and a spread of moderates below that. Little Russia, in Peskett Canyon, holds the most climbs: steep limestone sport routes, with the steeper, harder north side mostly in shade and the easier south side sunnier, about a 15 minute walk in. Other crags include The Dark Side, Kootenay Plains, Abraham Slabs and Boundary Bluffs.
